_about: Opening-repertoire builder. Every value here is a PLACEHOLDER chosen from chess reasoning, not fitted — the repertoire has no ground truth to fit against yet. Each carries a _comment saying what it is for and what would move it.
_comment_max_plies: PLACEHOLDER. 8 moves a side. Past this a line stops being a repertoire and becomes a middlegame you happen to have reached; the user's own games also thin out fast, so deeper nodes fail min_node_games anyway.
_comment_min_node_games: PLACEHOLDER. A position reached twice is a coincidence; three times is a habit. Below this the node is not yours and is not drilled.
_comment_min_branch_share: PLACEHOLDER. A reply you meet in under a quarter of the games from a node is an experiment, not part of the line. Keeps the extracted tree small enough to drill in five minutes.
_comment_max_branches: PLACEHOLDER. At most two continuations followed per node. The tree is for practice, not for completeness — fanning out to every legal reply produces hundreds of cards nobody finishes.
_comment_consistent_share: PLACEHOLDER. Below this share for your own most-played move, you have not decided what you play here — that is the `gap` verdict, and picking one move is the drill.
_comment_fix_delta_w: PLACEHOLDER, in win% lost per visit, averaged over the plies a review scored. 4 win% every time you reach a position you reach every fifth game is a real hole; under it, the move is a preference and not a leak.
_comment_score_prior_games: PLACEHOLDER. Shrinks a node's score toward 50% so 1-for-1 does not outrank 7-for-10 when choosing which move to recommend at a `gap`.
_comment_drill_recent_days: PLACEHOLDER. A card answered correctly within this many days is pushed to the back of the queue — enough to stop one session repeating itself, short enough that a weekly line still comes round.
_comment_verdict_weight: PLACEHOLDER ordering, not a measurement. Drill what you get wrong before what you merely play; the numbers only need to rank.
